# `fast-trend-vol` — development report

**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 only. The 2024-01-02 → 2026-10-23
holdout was not loaded, inspected or used for selection.
**Execution:** 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band, long-only,
weights ≥ 0 and sum ≤ 1.
**Bar:** TQQQ buy-and-hold, 2016-2023: **36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD /
0.82 Sharpe** (official 1-minute marks; this harness measures 36.15% / 82.29% /
0.80 on the same bars).

## Verdict

**PASS on the stated bar, with a serious whipsaw caveat.** The frozen base
earns **51.51% CAGR, 42.54% max DD and 1.20 Sharpe** at 1 bp on 1-minute
marks. It beats the TQQQ bar by **+14.79 pp of CAGR** with a drawdown
**39.75 pp lower**, and it is inside the 60% design-DD target. At 5 bp it is
49.70% / 43.00% / 1.17; at 10 bp it is 47.46% / 43.56% / 1.14. The 8-cell
pre-registered grid is a plateau (all 8 pass), and the 165-day QQQ SMA
baseline (benchmark only) is beaten on CAGR, drawdown and Sharpe.

The caveat is not cosmetic. The 42.54% max DD is a **2019 whipsaw**, and in
2019 the strategy returned +54.92% with a 42.54% DD while TQQQ returned
+148.23% with a 31.96% DD — worse on both return and drawdown. The full-period
pass is carried by the 2020 and 2023 recoveries and by avoiding 2022. This is
a crash-avoidance strategy that pays a large whipsaw cost in volatile bull
markets, not a uniformly superior TQQQ substitute.

The strategy is also **not** a low-correlation diversifier: daily-return
correlation to TQQQ is 0.666, because it carries a ~78% average TQQQ weight
and is long on ~80% of sessions. The edge is risk-managed TQQQ beta, not a new
return stream.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | **51.51%** | 49.70% | 47.46% |
| Max drawdown | **42.54%** | 43.00% | 43.56% |
| Sharpe | **1.20** | 1.17 | 1.14 |
| Sortino | 1.69 | 1.65 | 1.60 |
| Annualised vol | 42.19% | 42.18% | 42.18% |
| TQQQ exposure (mean weight) | 78.41% | 78.41% | 78.41% |
| Time in TQQQ | 79.75% | 79.75% | 79.75% |
| Fills | 374 | 374 | 370 |
| Turnover (× initial equity) | 1,765.0 | 1,652.2 | 1,521.0 |
| Correlation to TQQQ (daily) | 0.666 | 0.666 | 0.667 |
| Ending equity on $100k | $2,758,815 | $2,506,615 | $2,221,500 |

For reference, the same harness over the same bars:

| Asset | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TQQQ buy & hold | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 |
| QQQ buy & hold | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 |
| BIL buy & hold | 1.39% | 0.24% | 0.92 |
| 165-day QQQ SMA → TQQQ (benchmark only) | 43.60% | 59.64% | 1.00 |

The 165-day baseline is computed only for comparison; it is never an input
to `build_weights`. The official revisit figure for that baseline is 44.76% /
58.76%; either measurement is below the candidate.

## What the strategy does

Exact rules are in `HYPOTHESIS.md`; the short version:

1. **Two-speed daily trend.** Enter TQQQ when QQQ's 15:59 close is above its
   20-day EMA. Exit when QQQ's 15:59 close is 2.5% below its 50-day EMA. The
   2.5% buffer is hysteresis; the 20-day entry is the fast leg, the 50-day
   exit is the slow leg. No 165-day (or 100–250-day) moving average is used.
2. **Volatility target.** TQQQ weight is multiplied by
   `min(1, 0.85 / vol20)`, where `vol20` is annualised TQQQ daily-return
   volatility over the prior 20 sessions. The remainder is BIL.
3. **Daily crash cooldown.** After a QQQ daily log return ≤ −3.5%, go to BIL
   at the next open and stay out for 5 sessions.
4. **Intraday QQQ crash brake.** While long, if QQQ's 1-minute close falls
   2.5% below the session open, exit at the next minute and stay BIL for the
   rest of the session and the night. Re-enter at the next open if the daily
   target is still on. This is a **QQQ** 2.5% stop, not the old **TQQQ** 4%
   stop; a 4% QQQ stop is too wide to matter (ablation below).

The signal uses each session's **15:59 1-minute close**, not the official
16:00 daily close, so the decision is made with the price actually known at
15:59. The daily parquet is used only for the pre-2016 EMA/volatility warmup.
The truncation check confirms every weight before 2020-12-31 is unchanged
when all later data is removed.

## Results by year

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | TQQQ DD | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2016 | +7.71% | +19.86% | 38.10% | lag; missed part of the post-Brexit recovery |
| 2017 | +120.86% | +114.54% | 15.97% | win |
| 2018 | −18.67% | −20.76% | 58.62% | win, but a difficult whipsaw year |
| 2019 | +54.92% | +148.23% | 31.96% | **whipsaw: 42.5% DD vs TQQQ's 32.0%; −93 pp return** |
| 2020 | +178.48% | +104.14% | 72.74% | win; crash brakes and April re-entry |
| 2021 | +53.82% | +81.05% | 32.84% | lag |
| 2022 | −28.80% | −79.39% | 81.10% | win; trend exit avoided the bear, but rallies hurt |
| 2023 | +177.17% | +192.05% | 34.93% | slight lag |

The profile is crash avoidance, not consistent alpha: the strategy beats TQQQ
in 4 of 8 years, but the 2020 win (+74.3 pp) and the 2022 win (+50.6 pp)
dominate. The 2019 lag (−93.3 pp) is the largest single-year opportunity cost,
and it came with a larger drawdown than TQQQ.

Log-P&L shares: 2020 31.7%, 2023 31.6%, 2017 24.5%, 2019 13.5%, 2021 13.3%,
2016 2.3%; 2018 −6.4%, 2022 −10.5%. No single year contributes more than 80%
of the total, but 2020 + 2023 contribute 63% and the result is clearly helped
by the two recovery years.

## The 2019 whipsaw (the real failure mode)

The 42.54% max DD runs **2019-04-29 14:44 → 2019-10-03 10:08**. It is not a
crash drawdown; it is the cost of the fast entry and the crash brakes in a
volatile, range-bound bull market.

August 2019 daily illustration (strategy return, TQQQ return, daily target
weight for the session):

| Date | Strategy | TQQQ | Session target | What happened |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2019-08-02 | −4.22% | −4.22% | 1.00 | long into the drop |
| 2019-08-05 | −10.85% | −10.85% | 1.00 | long into the crash |
| 2019-08-06 | +2.87% | +4.31% | 0.00 | sold at the open after the gap; missed the intraday rebound |
| 2019-08-08 | 0.00% | +6.90% | 0.00 | flat; missed the rebound |
| 2019-08-14 | −4.44% | −9.15% | 1.00 | re-entered into the next drop |
| 2019-08-23 | −9.52% | −9.25% | 1.00 | long into the next drop |
| 2019-08-26 | 0.00% | +4.19% | 0.00 | sold at the bottom; missed the rebound |

The pattern is classic whipsaw: sell the low, miss the rebound, re-enter before
the next drop. In 2019 the strategy returned +54.9% with a 42.5% DD while TQQQ
returned +148.2% with a 32.0% DD. A range-bound, high-volatility bull market is
the worst regime for this design. The 2018 loss (−18.7%) and the 2022 loss
(−28.8%) are smaller problems by comparison.

|---|---:|

| 2016-06-24 | −12.17% |
| 2020-09-03 | −12.11% |
| 2020-02-24 | −11.64% |
| 2020-10-28 | −11.60% |

These are mostly overnight gaps or days when the intraday QQQ stop did not
trigger before the close. The strategy has no overnight gap protection; the
daily crash cooldown only acts at the next open. This is a structural
limitation, not a bug.

## Why it works, and where it could fail

**Why it works.** TQQQ's 82% drawdown is a multi-month bear-market phenomenon,
not a single-day phenomenon. The 50-day exit with a 2.5% buffer leaves 2018Q4,
2020 and 2022; the 20-day entry re-enters the recovery. The crash brakes cut
the first days of a shock and the 2.5% QQQ stop catches the intraday
continuation of a market-wide sell-off. The strategy retains a ~78% average
TQQQ weight and is long on ~80% of sessions, so it keeps most of the drift.

**Where it could fail.**

- **Whipsaw is the dominant risk, and 2019 is the proof.** The strategy sold
  the May and August 2019 lows, missed the rebounds, and re-entered before the
  next drop. It returned +54.9% vs TQQQ's +148.2% and had a 42.5% DD vs
  TQQQ's 32.0%. A choppy, high-volatility bull market is worse for this
  strategy than a clean bear market.
- **2020 V-recovery.** The 50-day exit is slow; the 20-day entry and the
  5-session cooldown can re-enter too late. The strategy still earned 178.5%
  in 2020, but part of that is the April–August trend, not the bottom.
- **Intraday stop at the low.** A 2.5% QQQ break can be a stop-run that
  reverses; the stop sells near the low and misses the rebound. The 34 stop
  events over 8 years are a small sample; the parameter is a round-number
  centre, not a fitted optimum.
- **Overnight gaps.** The largest losses are gap days. The daily cooldown
  cannot avoid the gap itself.
- **Costs.** 374 fills and 1,765× turnover. At 10 bp the CAGR is 47.46% —
  still a pass, but 4 pp below the 1 bp headline.
- **Concentration.** 2020 and 2023 contribute 63% of the log P&L, and the
  2016–2019 sub-period is below the bar. The point estimate should be treated
  as high-40s to low-50s CAGR, not a guaranteed 51.5%.

## How this differs from the existing strategies

| Existing strategy | Mechanism | Difference |
|---|---|---|
| `daily-regime-minute-entry` (round-1 winner) | 165-day QQQ SMA + armed 4% **TQQQ** stop | 20/50-day EMA, no 165-day SMA, **QQQ** 2.5% stop, 85% vol target |
| `vol-scaled-crash-stop` | always-long TQQQ, inverse-ATR size, ATR barrier | trend-gated; BIL when the trend is off |
| `dynamic-leverage-throttle` | episodic post-vol-shock recovery in BIL during calm uptrends | owns calm uptrends; de-risks in shocks |
| `dual-speed-regime` | 60-minute intraday EMA, flat overnight | daily decisions, holds overnight |
| `donchian-breakout` | 5-minute 20/55/390 alignment ladder, QQQ sleeve, ATR sizing | daily 20/50 EMA, TQQQ/BIL, vol target |
| `ratio-froth`, `ratio-pairs` | TQQQ/QQQ ratio signals | no ratio |
| `drawdown-regime` | post-drawdown recovery windows | continuous trend state |

The combination — daily 20/50 EMA, 85% vol target, QQQ 2.5% intraday stop,
−3.5%/5 daily crash cooldown — is not used by any existing strategy. The
strategy also deliberately avoids the old 4% TQQQ stop: a 4% **QQQ** stop is
too wide (ablation 45.29% / 44.64%, essentially the no-stop result), so the
2.5% QQQ threshold is doing real work and is not a re-skin of the old winner.

## Falsifier checklist

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CAGR ≤ 36.72% or DD ≥ 82.29% | 51.51% / 42.54% | **pass** |
| 2 | Fewer than 6/8 grid cells pass, or isolated peak | 8/8 pass; base not the best cell | **pass** |
| 3 | 10 bp CAGR ≤ 36.72% | 47.46% | **pass** |
| 4 | Lag/placebo matches the base | lag 10/20 collapse; base 93rd pct CAGR, 100th pct Sharpe; one placebo CAGR higher | **mostly pass** |
| 5 | One year >80% of P&L, or both halves negative | no year >80%; 2016–2019 +32.7%, 2022–2023 +40.8% | **pass, with early-half caveat** |
| 6 | 165-day baseline beats it on CAGR and DD | 43.60% / 59.64% vs 51.51% / 42.54% | **pass** |
| 7 | Core without the intraday stop ≤ 36.72% | 45.26% | **pass** (stop is not the only source) |
| 8 | Truncation changes prior weights | daily max diff 0.0; 1m prefix identical | **pass** |

## Bottom line

The strategy passes the stated development bar comfortably:
**51.51% CAGR, 42.54% max DD, 1.20 Sharpe at 1 bp**, with a broad 8-cell

risk-managed TQQQ allocator with a real crash-avoidance edge, not a
low-correlation alpha stream and not a uniformly better TQQQ.

# Hypothesis and pre-registration — `fast-trend-vol`

**Status:** frozen for the final 1-minute development evaluation.
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 only. The 2024-01-02 →
2026-10-23 holdout is not loaded, inspected or used for selection.
**Universe:** QQQ (signal), TQQQ (long), BIL (cash). Long-only, weights ≥ 0,
sum ≤ 1.
**Execution:** weights set at the close of a 1-minute bar fill at the next
bar's open; 2% band; 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp sensitivity.

## 1. Mechanism

TQQQ's problem is not its average return, it is its path: 3× daily resetting
turns a multi-month QQQ bear market into an 80% drawdown, and high realised
volatility imposes a geometric drag. A fast trend state can own TQQQ while the
trend is up, stand aside during the multi-month bears, and re-enter quickly
after a V-shaped recovery. A volatility target reduces exposure exactly when
TQQQ's own realised volatility is high, which is when both the drag and the
left tail are largest.

The strategy is a **two-speed daily EMA trend** with a **volatility budget**
and two **crash brakes**:

- The **fast leg** (20-day EMA) decides when to enter. It is quick enough to
  participate in the recovery after a crash.
- The **slow leg** (50-day EMA) with a 2.5% exit buffer decides when to leave.
  The buffer is hysteresis: a normal pullback through the 50-day line does not
  force an exit, but a 2.5% break does.
- The **volatility target** sizes TQQQ at `min(1, 0.85 / vol20)`, where `vol20`
  is annualised TQQQ daily-return volatility over the prior 20 sessions.
- The **daily crash brake** exits after a QQQ daily log return ≤ −3.5% and
  stays out for the next 5 sessions.
- The **intraday crash brake** exits if QQQ's 1-minute close falls 2.5% below
  the session open while the book is long, and stays out for the rest of the
  session and the night. QQQ is the signal asset; a 2.5% QQQ fall is roughly a
  7.5% TQQQ fall. This is deliberately **not** the old 4% TQQQ stop.

## 2. Exact rules

Let `Q_t` be QQQ's adjusted daily close, taken as the **15:59 1-minute
close** of session `t` (the price actually known at the decision time), and
`E20_t` and `E50_t` its 20- and
50-session EMAs (all data through the close of session `t`). Let `S_t` be the
trend state:

```
S_t = 0 initially
if S_{t-1} = 0 and Q_t > E20_t:        S_t = 1     # fast entry
elif S_{t-1} = 1 and Q_t < 0.975*E50_t: S_t = 0     # slow exit with 2.5% buffer
else:                                   S_t = S_{t-1}
```

Let `r_t = ln(Q_t/Q_{t-1})`, `v_t` = annualised standard deviation of TQQQ
daily log returns over the last 20 sessions, and `C_t` the crash cooldown:

```
if r_t <= -0.035: cooldown = 5
C_t = 1 if cooldown > 0 else 0
cooldown = max(0, cooldown - 1)
```

Daily target:

```
w_t = S_t * (1 - C_t) * min(1, 0.85 / v_t)     # TQQQ weight
BIL weight = 1 - w_t
```

Intraday override, for each session `k` with open `O_k`:

```
if the book is long at the session open and QQQ 1m close < 0.975 * O_k:
    exit TQQQ at the next 1m open
    stay BIL for the rest of session k and the night
    re-enter at session k+1's open at w_k (the daily target known at k's close)
```

No 165-day (or any 100–250-day) moving average is used. The only slow filter
is the 50-day EMA, which is the upper end of the mandated 5–50 day range.

## 3. Why it should beat buy-and-hold TQQQ

1. **Crash avoidance.** TQQQ's 82% drawdown is made by 2018Q4, 2020 and 2022.
   The 50-day exit with a 2.5% buffer leaves those regimes; the 20-day entry
   re-enters after the recovery. The daily and intraday crash brakes cut the
   first days of a shock, when the compounding damage is largest.
2. **Volatility drag.** TQQQ's geometric return is hurt by high realised
   volatility. Sizing down when `vol20 > 85%` cuts exposure in exactly the
   high-variance periods that produce the deepest drawdowns.
3. **Retained upside.** The strategy carries a ~78% average TQQQ weight and is
   long on ~80% of sessions, so it keeps most of the drift. It gives up some
   melt-up beta (2019, 2021) in exchange for crash protection.
4. **No free lunch assumed.** The 2% band, next-open fills and 1/5/10 bp costs
   are all charged. The strategy does not use shorting or leverage beyond
   TQQQ's embedded 3×.

## 4. Why it could fail

- **Whipsaw.** 2018 and 2022 had repeated false recoveries. A fast entry can
  re-enter into a bear-market rally and take another loss. The 50-day buffer
  helps but does not eliminate this.
- **2020 V-recovery.** The 50-day exit is slow to re-enter after the crash.
  The 20-day entry helps, but if the recovery is faster than the 20-day EMA the
  strategy lags. The 5-session daily cooldown can also delay re-entry.
- **Intraday stop at the low.** A 2.5% QQQ intraday break can be a stop-run
  that reverses; the stop then sells near the low and misses the rebound.
- **Cost and turnover.** About 370 fills and 1,780× cumulative turnover. At
  10 bp the CAGR is lower; if the edge is cost-fragile it should be rejected.
- **Concentration.** 2020 and 2023 are strong recovery years. If the result is
  carried by one of them, the point estimate is not representative.

## 5. Falsifiers (decided before the final run)

1. **Bar:** dev CAGR ≤ 36.72%, or dev max DD ≥ 82.29%. The design target is
   DD < 60%; a DD between 60% and 82.29% is a technical pass but not a good
   risk result.
2. **Plateau:** fewer than 6 of the 8 pre-registered cells pass the bar, or the
   base cell is an isolated peak rather than inside a neighbourhood.
3. **Costs:** 10 bp CAGR ≤ 36.72%.
4. **Placebo:** a 5/10/20-session lag of the daily signal, or a shuffled-run
   placebo with the same exposure and persistence, matches the base's CAGR and
   Sharpe. The timing must add something.
5. **Concentration:** one calendar year contributes more than 80% of total
   P&L, or both 2016–2019 and 2022–2023 are negative.
6. **Baseline:** the 165-day QQQ SMA baseline (benchmark only, never an input)
   beats the strategy on both CAGR and max DD over the same window.
7. **Core ablation:** removing the intraday crash stop drops CAGR to ≤ 36.72%
   (i.e., the trend + vol + daily-crash core is not enough on its own).
8. **Causality:** truncating the data at a cut date changes any weight before
   the cut.

## 6. Pre-registered parameter grid (8 cells)

The base is the centre of the design, not the best cell found by a search.
Each other cell moves one parameter by one step.

| Cell | Entry EMA | Exit EMA | Exit buffer | Vol target | Intraday QQQ stop | Daily crash |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **base** | 20 | 50 | 2.5% | 85% | 2.5% | −3.5% / 5 sessions |
| `buf_2.0` | 20 | 50 | 2.0% | 85% | 2.5% | −3.5% / 5 |
| `buf_3.0` | 20 | 50 | 3.0% | 85% | 2.5% | −3.5% / 5 |
| `entry_15` | 15 | 50 | 2.5% | 85% | 2.5% | −3.5% / 5 |
| `entry_25` | 25 | 50 | 2.5% | 85% | 2.5% | −3.5% / 5 |
| `tv_0.70` | 20 | 50 | 2.5% | 70% | 2.5% | −3.5% / 5 |
| `istop_2.0` | 20 | 50 | 2.5% | 85% | 2.0% | −3.5% / 5 |
| `istop_3.0` | 20 | 50 | 2.5% | 85% | 3.0% | −3.5% / 5 |

The daily crash threshold is held at −3.5% / 5 sessions in the grid; its
neighbourhood is reported separately as a robustness check. The exit EMA is
held at 50; the entry EMA moves 15/20/25. Every cell is a complete strategy
with the same execution, costs and universe.

## 7. Expected effect (design target, not a result)

- CAGR in the 40–50% range, max DD in the 35–50% range, Sharpe around 1.0–1.2.
- TQQQ exposure around 75–80% of sessions, daily-return correlation to TQQQ
  around 0.6–0.7 (high, because it is still a TQQQ allocator, but lower than
  buy-and-hold's 1.0).
- The pass condition is strict: **CAGR > 36.72% and max DD < 82.29%**, with
  DD < 60% as the design target. A lower-CAGR but much better Sharpe/Calmar
  result would be reported as risk-adjusted, not as a pass.

## 8. How this differs from the existing strategies

- **`daily-regime-minute-entry` (round-1 winner):** 165-day QQQ SMA + an armed
  4% **TQQQ** stop. This strategy uses a 20/50-day EMA pair (no 165-day SMA),
  an 85% volatility target, a **QQQ** 2.5% intraday stop, and a daily −3.5%
  crash cooldown. It does not use the 4% TQQQ stop.
- **`vol-scaled-crash-stop`:** always-long TQQQ at inverse-ATR size with an
  ATR barrier; no trend gate. This strategy is trend-gated and sits in BIL when
  the trend is off.
- **`dynamic-leverage-throttle` (VSR):** episodic post-vol-shock recovery,
  deliberately in BIL during calm uptrends. This strategy is the opposite: it
  owns calm uptrends and de-risks in shocks.
- **`dual-speed-regime`:** 60-minute intraday EMA, flat overnight. This
  strategy makes daily decisions and holds overnight.
- **`donchian-breakout`:** 5-minute 20/55/390 alignment ladder, QQQ sleeve,
  ATR sizing. This strategy is daily 20/50 EMA, TQQQ/BIL, volatility-targeted.
- **`ratio-froth` / `ratio-pairs`:** TQQQ/QQQ ratio signals. This strategy
  uses no ratio.
- **`drawdown-regime`:** post-drawdown recovery windows. This strategy uses a
  continuous trend state, not a drawdown-triggered window.

No existing strategy uses the daily 20/50 EMA + 85% vol target + QQQ 2.5%
intraday stop + −3.5% daily crash cooldown combination.

## 9. Data discipline and causality

- Signal prices are the adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ **15:59 session closes**
  from the dev panel. The local adjusted daily parquet is used only for the
  pre-2016 EMA/volatility warmup, filtered to dates before 2016-01-04.
- Execution and marks come from the adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel,
  truncated at 2023-12-29.
- Every weight at session `t` uses only closes through 15:59 of `t`; the
  last-bar mapping fills the next session's open. The official 16:00 daily
  close is not used at 15:59, so there is no one-minute look-ahead.
- The causality check rebuilds the daily target with data truncated at
  2020-12-31 and confirms that every weight before the cut is unchanged.
- No full-sample normalisation, no future data in any rolling window, no
  holdout inspection.

## 10. Design provenance (honest note)

The strategy family was calibrated on the daily development panel before this
pre-registration. The final 8-cell grid above and the 1-minute evaluation were
frozen before the final `strategy.py` run. The report contains the full grid,
the ablation and placebo results, and the negative evidence, not only the best
cell. The design choices (20/50 EMA, 2.5% buffer, 85% vol target, 2.5% QQQ
stop, −3.5%/5 daily crash) are round-number centres of the explored
neighbourhood, not the single best values from a search.

**Implementation note (post-freeze causality fix, 2026-11-27).** The first
1-minute evaluation used the official 16:00 daily close at the 15:59 bar,
which is a one-minute look-ahead. The final run uses the 15:59 1-minute close.
The frozen grid and parameters were unchanged. The causal fix reduced the
1 bp CAGR from 51.70% to 51.51% and moved the max-drawdown episode from a
January–May 2018 whipsaw (41.47%) to an April–October 2019 whipsaw (42.54%).
The final `result.json` and `report.md` reflect the causal 15:59 run.

## What the strategy does

Exact rules are in `HYPOTHESIS.md`; the short version:

1. **Two-speed daily trend.** Enter TQQQ when QQQ's 15:59 close is above its
   20-day EMA. Exit when QQQ's 15:59 close is 2.5% below its 50-day EMA. The
   2.5% buffer is hysteresis; the 20-day entry is the fast leg, the 50-day
   exit is the slow leg. No 165-day (or 100–250-day) moving average is used.
2. **Volatility target.** TQQQ weight is multiplied by
   `min(1, 0.85 / vol20)`, where `vol20` is annualised TQQQ daily-return
   volatility over the prior 20 sessions. The remainder is BIL.
3. **Daily crash cooldown.** After a QQQ daily log return ≤ −3.5%, go to BIL
   at the next open and stay out for 5 sessions.
4. **Intraday QQQ crash brake.** While long, if QQQ's 1-minute close falls
   2.5% below the session open, exit at the next minute and stay BIL for the
   rest of the session and the night. Re-enter at the next open if the daily
   target is still on. This is a **QQQ** 2.5% stop, not the old **TQQQ** 4%
   stop; a 4% QQQ stop is too wide to matter (ablation below).

The signal uses each session's **15:59 1-minute close**, not the official
16:00 daily close, so the decision is made with the price actually known at
15:59. The daily parquet is used only for the pre-2016 EMA/volatility warmup.
The truncation check confirms every weight before 2020-12-31 is unchanged
when all later data is removed.

DEVELOPMENT WINDOW ONLY: 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29.  The 2024-2026 holdout is
never loaded by this script.

Idea
----
TQQQ's 3x daily reset makes multi-month bear markets catastrophic and makes
high realised volatility expensive.  A two-speed daily EMA trend owns TQQQ in
uptrends and sits in BIL otherwise; an 85% volatility target cuts exposure when
TQQQ's own realised volatility is high; a QQQ 2.5% intraday crash brake and a
QQQ -3.5% daily crash cooldown cut the first days of a shock.

No 165-day (or any 100-250 day) moving average is used.  No 4% TQQQ stop.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    python research/new/fast-trend-vol/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BARS = 252 * 390
SYMBOLS = ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL")
TZ = "America/New_York"

# Frozen base (centre of the pre-registered grid, not the best cell).
BASE = dict(
    entry=20,
    exit_=50,
    buffer=0.025,
    target_vol=0.85,
    vol_window=20,
    crash_thr=-0.035,
    crash_cd=5,
    intraday_stop=0.025,
)

GRID = {
    "base": dict(BASE),
    "buf_2.0": dict(BASE, buffer=0.020),
    "buf_3.0": dict(BASE, buffer=0.030),
    "entry_15": dict(BASE, entry=15),
    "entry_25": dict(BASE, entry=25),
    "tv_0.70": dict(BASE, target_vol=0.70),
    "istop_2.0": dict(BASE, intraday_stop=0.020),
    "istop_3.0": dict(BASE, intraday_stop=0.030),
}

_DAILY_CACHE: dict = {}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# daily signal data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def load_prehistory(before_date):
    """Adjusted QQQ/TQQQ daily closes strictly before the first 1m session.

    Used only to warm the EMAs/volatility before 2016-01-04.  The signal for
    every session in the panel uses that session's 15:59 1-minute close, not
    the official 16:00 daily close, so the decision is made with the price
    actually known at 15:59.
    """
    key = ("pre", before_date)
    if key in _DAILY_CACHE:
        return _DAILY_CACHE[key]
    q = pd.read_parquet(ROOT / "data" / "intraday-hf" / "QQQ-1d-yahoo.parquet")
    q["date"] = pd.to_datetime(q["date"]).dt.date
    q = q[q["date"] < before_date].sort_values("date")
    t = pd.read_parquet(ROOT / "data" / "intraday-hf" / "TQQQ-1d-yahoo.parquet")
    t["date"] = pd.to_datetime(t["date"]).dt.date
    t = t[t["date"] < before_date].sort_values("date")
    if not (q["date"].to_numpy() == t["date"].to_numpy()).all():
        raise RuntimeError("QQQ/TQQQ daily calendars differ")
    out = (q["date"].to_numpy(),
           q["adjclose"].astype(float).to_numpy(),
           t["adjclose"].astype(float).to_numpy())
    _DAILY_CACHE[key] = out
    return out


def panel_daily(ts, o, c):
    """Daily closes from the 1m panel's 15:59 bars, plus pre-2016 warmup."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    sess = dates[last]
    pre_dates, pre_q, pre_t = load_prehistory(sess[0])
    return (np.concatenate([pre_dates, sess]),
            np.concatenate([pre_q, c[last, 0]]),
            np.concatenate([pre_t, c[last, 1]]))


def daily_target(dates, q, tq, entry=20, exit_=50, buffer=0.025,
                 target_vol=0.85, vol_window=20, crash_thr=-0.035, crash_cd=5):
    """Daily TQQQ target and its components, all through the current close."""
    e_entry = pd.Series(q).ewm(span=entry, adjust=False).mean().to_numpy()
    e_exit = pd.Series(q).ewm(span=exit_, adjust=False).mean().to_numpy()
    rq = np.diff(np.log(q), prepend=np.log(q[0]))

    state = np.zeros(len(q))
    on = 0
    for k in range(len(q)):
        if on == 0 and q[k] > e_entry[k]:
            on = 1
        elif on == 1 and q[k] < e_exit[k] * (1.0 - buffer):
            on = 0
        state[k] = float(on)

    crash = np.zeros(len(q))
    left = 0
    for k in range(len(q)):
        if rq[k] <= crash_thr:
            left = crash_cd
        crash[k] = 1.0 if left > 0 else 0.0
        left = max(0, left - 1)

    rt = np.diff(np.log(tq), prepend=np.log(tq[0]))
    vol = pd.Series(rt).rolling(vol_window, min_periods=vol_window).std().to_numpy() * np.sqrt(252.0)
    vt = np.clip(target_vol / np.maximum(vol, 1e-6), 0.0, 1.0)
    w = state * (1.0 - crash) * vt
    return dict(w=np.nan_to_num(w, nan=0.0), state=state, crash=crash,
                vol=vol, vt=np.nan_to_num(vt, nan=0.0),
                e20=e_entry, e50=e_exit)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# daily target -> 1-minute weights
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def map_to_minute(ts, daily_dates, w_daily, o, c, intraday_stop=0.025):
    """Causal daily-target -> 1m weight mapping.

    For each session k:
      * bars except the last carry the target known at the previous close;
      * the last bar carries the target computed at session k's close, which
        fills at session k+1's open.
    The intraday QQQ stop overrides the rest of the session and the night;
    the next open re-enters at the daily target if it is still on.
    """
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    wd = pd.Series(w_daily, index=pd.Index(daily_dates))
    wd = wd[~wd.index.duplicated(keep="last")]
    ws = wd.reindex(pd.Index(dates[last])).ffill().fillna(0.0).to_numpy()

    W = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    for k in range(len(first)):
        prev = ws[k - 1] if k > 0 else 0.0
        f, l = first[k], last[k]
        W[f:l, 1] = prev
        W[l, 1] = ws[k]
        W[f:l, 2] = 1.0 - prev
        W[l, 2] = 1.0 - ws[k]

    n_stops = 0
    if intraday_stop and intraday_stop > 0:
        for k in range(len(first)):
            f, l = first[k], last[k]
            if W[f, 1] <= 0:
                continue
            trigger = o[f, 0] * (1.0 - intraday_stop)
            idx = np.flatnonzero(c[f:l + 1, 0] < trigger)
            if len(idx) == 0:
                continue
            i = f + int(idx[0])
            W[i:l, 1] = 0.0
            W[i:l, 2] = 1.0
            if i < l:
                # re-enter at the next open at the target known at this close
                W[l, 1] = ws[k]
                W[l, 2] = 1.0 - ws[k]
            else:
                # a last-bar trigger can only fill at the next open; stay BIL
                # for that open and let the next session's first bar re-enter.
                W[l, 1] = 0.0
                W[l, 2] = 1.0
            n_stops += 1
    return W, n_stops


def target_from_params(dates, q, tq, p):
    return daily_target(dates, q, tq, entry=p["entry"], exit_=p["exit_"],
                        buffer=p["buffer"], target_vol=p["target_vol"],
                        vol_window=p.get("vol_window", 20),
                        crash_thr=p["crash_thr"], crash_cd=p["crash_cd"])


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None):
    """Required entry point: QQQ/TQQQ/BIL 1m panel -> (n,3) weights."""
    p = dict(BASE)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    dates, q, tq = panel_daily(ts, o, c)
    d = target_from_params(dates, q, tq, p)
    W, _ = map_to_minute(ts, dates, d["w"], o, c, p["intraday_stop"])
    return W


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _ts(x):
    return pd.Timestamp(x, tz=TZ)


def daily_returns(ts, equity):
    _, _, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    eq = equity[last]
    dates = bt.session_dates(ts)[last]
    return pd.Series(np.diff(eq) / eq[:-1], index=pd.Index(dates[1:]))


def seg_stats(r, a, b):
    """CAGR / max DD / Sharpe on the [a, b) slice of a simulation result."""
    t, e = r["ts"], r["equity"]
    m = (t >= _ts(a)) & (t < _ts(b))
    e = e[m]
    t = t[m]
    if len(e) < 2:
        return None
    years = (t[-1] - t[0]).total_seconds() / (365.25 * 86400.0)
    rets = np.diff(e) / e[:-1]
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(e)
    return dict(
        cagr=float((e[-1] / e[0]) ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0),
        max_drawdown=float(-(e / peak - 1.0).min()),
        sharpe=float(np.mean(rets) / np.std(rets) * np.sqrt(BARS)) if np.std(rets) > 0 else 0.0,
    )


def metrics(ts, o, c, W, start=DEV_START, slip=1.0):
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, W, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    s = bt.stats(r, BARS)
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, start)
    eq = r["equity"]

    # daily correlation to TQQQ buy-and-hold
    _, _, last = bt.day_bounds(r["ts"])
    deq = eq[last]
    dtq = c[i0:][last, 1]
    dr = np.diff(deq) / deq[:-1]
    tr = np.diff(dtq) / dtq[:-1]
    corr = float(np.corrcoef(dr, tr)[0, 1]) if len(dr) > 2 else 0.0

    # max-drawdown episode
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    dd = eq / peak - 1.0
    trough = int(np.argmin(dd))
    peak_i = int(np.argmax(eq[:trough + 1]))

    # worst 5 days
    daily = daily_returns(r["ts"], eq)
    worst = daily.nsmallest(5)

    yearly = {}
    y = r["ts"].year
    for yy in range(2016, 2024):
        m = y == yy
        if m.any():
            yearly[str(yy)] = float(eq[m][-1] / eq[m][0] - 1.0)

    return dict(
        cagr=float(s["cagr"]),
        max_drawdown=float(s["max_drawdown"]),
        sharpe=float(s["sharpe"]),
        sortino=float(s["sortino"]),
        volatility=float(s["volatility"]),
        calibrated_exposure=float(s["exposure"]),  # 1.0 when BIL is an asset
        tqqq_exposure=float(np.mean(W[i0:, 1])),
        time_in_tqqq=float(np.mean(W[i0:, 1] > 1e-9)),
        fills=int(s["fills"]),
        turnover=float(s["turnover"]),
        corr_tqqq=corr,
        yearly=yearly,
        max_dd_peak=str(r["ts"][peak_i]),
        max_dd_trough=str(r["ts"][trough]),
        worst_days={str(k): float(v) for k, v in worst.items()},
        ending_equity=float(s["ending_equity"]),
        years=float(s["years"]),
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# robustness helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def shuffle_runs(state, rng):
    """Permute the run-length sequence; preserve on/off days and persistence."""
    idx = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, state[1:] != state[:-1]])
    lengths = np.diff(np.r_[idx, len(state)])
    vals = state[idx]
    order = rng.permutation(len(lengths))
    out = np.concatenate([np.full(int(lengths[j]), float(vals[j])) for j in order])
    return out[:len(state)]


def baseline_165d(ts, o, c):
    """Old daily 165-day QQQ SMA regime, benchmark only (never an input)."""
    dates, q, _ = panel_daily(ts, o, c)
    sma = pd.Series(q).rolling(165).mean().to_numpy()
    reg = np.where(np.isfinite(sma) & (q > sma), 1.0, 0.0)
    W, _ = map_to_minute(ts, dates, reg, o, c, intraday_stop=0.0)
    return W


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def main():
    t0 = time.time()
    ts, o, c = bt.panel(SYMBOLS, DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min", warmup_days=0)
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, DEV_START)
    print(f"panel {len(ts):,} bars {ts[0]} .. {ts[-1]}  ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)")

    dates, q, tq = panel_daily(ts, o, c)
    base_d = target_from_params(dates, q, tq, BASE)
    W_base, n_stops = map_to_minute(ts, dates, base_d["w"], o, c,
                                    BASE["intraday_stop"])
    print(f"base: tqqq time {np.mean(W_base[i0:,1])*100:.1f}%  intraday stops {n_stops}")

    # primary at 1/5/10 bp
    primary = {}
    for slip in (1.0, 5.0, 10.0):
        primary[f"{slip:.0f}bp"] = metrics(ts, o, c, W_base, DEV_START, slip)

          f"Sharpe {primary['1bp']['sharpe']:.2f}  fills {primary['1bp']['fills']}")

    # 8-cell grid
    grid_W, grid_out = [], {}
    for name, p in GRID.items():
        d = target_from_params(dates, q, tq, p)
        W, ns = map_to_minute(ts, dates, d["w"], o, c, p["intraday_stop"])
        grid_W.append(W)
        grid_out[name] = dict(params=p, stops=ns)
    grid_res = bt.run_many(ts, o, c, grid_W, DEV_START, band=0.02,
                           slippage_bps=1.0, threads=1)
    for name, W, r in zip(GRID, grid_W, grid_res):
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS)
        grid_out[name].update(dict(cagr=float(s["cagr"]),
                                   max_drawdown=float(s["max_drawdown"]),
                                   sharpe=float(s["sharpe"]),
                                   tqqq_exposure=float(np.mean(W[i0:, 1])),
                                   fills=int(s["fills"])))
    print("grid done")

    # ablations (all 1 bp)
    ablations = {}
    variants = {
        "no_intraday_stop": dict(intraday_stop=0.0),
        "no_daily_crash": dict(crash_thr=-99.0),
        "no_crash_at_all": dict(intraday_stop=0.0, crash_thr=-99.0),
        "no_vol_target": dict(target_vol=99.0),
        "fast_exit_ema20": dict(exit_=20),
        "slow_entry_ema50": dict(entry=50),
        "wide_intraday_4pct": dict(intraday_stop=0.040),
    }
    for name, over in variants.items():
        p = dict(BASE)
        p.update(over)
        d = target_from_params(dates, q, tq, p)
        W, ns = map_to_minute(ts, dates, d["w"], o, c, p["intraday_stop"])
        ablations[name] = dict(params=p, stops=ns, **{
            k: v for k, v in metrics(ts, o, c, W, DEV_START, 1.0).items()
            if k in ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "tqqq_exposure", "fills",
                     "turnover", "corr_tqqq")})
    print("ablations done")

    # one-step neighbourhoods outside the pre-registered 8-cell grid
    neighbourhood = {}
    extra = {
        "crash_3.0": dict(crash_thr=-0.030),
        "crash_4.0": dict(crash_thr=-0.040),
        "crash_4.5": dict(crash_thr=-0.045),
        "exit_ema40": dict(exit_=40),
        "exit_ema60": dict(exit_=60),
        "volwin_15": dict(vol_window=15),
        "volwin_30": dict(vol_window=30),
    }
    for name, over in extra.items():
        p = dict(BASE)
        p.update(over)
        d = target_from_params(dates, q, tq, p)
        W, ns = map_to_minute(ts, dates, d["w"], o, c, p["intraday_stop"])
        m = metrics(ts, o, c, W, DEV_START, 1.0)
        neighbourhood[name] = dict(params=p, stops=ns, **{
            k: m[k] for k in ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe",
                              "tqqq_exposure", "fills")})
    print("neighbourhood done")

    # 165-day benchmark (benchmark only)
    W_165 = baseline_165d(ts, o, c)
    bench_165 = metrics(ts, o, c, W_165, DEV_START, 1.0)

    # lag placebo: shift the whole daily target by n sessions
    lag_out = {}
    for lag in (1, 5, 10, 20):
        wl = np.r_[np.zeros(lag), base_d["w"][:-lag]] if lag > 0 else base_d["w"]
        Wl, _ = map_to_minute(ts, dates, wl, o, c, BASE["intraday_stop"])
        m = metrics(ts, o, c, Wl, DEV_START, 1.0)
        lag_out[f"lag_{lag}"] = {k: m[k] for k in
                                 ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "tqqq_exposure")}
    print("lags done")

    # random-run placebo: same on/off days and persistence, random timing
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20261127)
    placebo = []
    for b in range(30):
        st = shuffle_runs(base_d["state"], rng)
        w = st * (1.0 - base_d["crash"]) * base_d["vt"]
        Wp, _ = map_to_minute(ts, dates, w, o, c, BASE["intraday_stop"])
        r = bt.run(ts, o, c, Wp, DEV_START, band=0.02, slippage_bps=1.0)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS)
        placebo.append(dict(cagr=float(s["cagr"]),
                            max_drawdown=float(s["max_drawdown"]),
                            sharpe=float(s["sharpe"])))
    pc = np.array([x["cagr"] for x in placebo])
    pd_ = np.array([x["max_drawdown"] for x in placebo])
    ps = np.array([x["sharpe"] for x in placebo])
    placebo_summary = dict(
        draws=len(placebo),
        cagr_median=float(np.median(pc)), cagr_p90=float(np.percentile(pc, 90)),
        cagr_max=float(pc.max()),
        dd_median=float(np.median(pd_)), dd_min=float(pd_.min()),
        sharpe_median=float(np.median(ps)), sharpe_max=float(ps.max()),
        base_cagr_percentile=float(np.mean(pc < primary["1bp"]["cagr"])),
        base_sharpe_percentile=float(np.mean(ps < primary["1bp"]["sharpe"])),
    )
    print("placebo done")

    # cut tests: fresh start at later dates
    cuts = {}
    for start in ("2017-01-03", "2018-01-02", "2019-01-02",
                  "2020-01-02", "2021-01-04", "2022-01-03"):
        s = metrics(ts, o, c, W_base, start, 1.0)
        cuts[start] = {k: s[k] for k in
                       ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "tqqq_exposure", "years")}

    # fixed sub-periods
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, W_base, DEV_START, band=0.02, slippage_bps=1.0)
    sub = {}
    for name, a, b in (("2016_2019", "2016-01-04", "2020-01-01"),
                       ("2020_2021", "2020-01-01", "2022-01-01"),
                       ("2022_2023", "2022-01-01", "2024-01-01")):
        sub[name] = seg_stats(r, a, b)

    # causality / truncation check
    ts_cut, o_cut, c_cut = bt.panel(SYMBOLS, DEV_START, "2020-12-31", "1min",
                                    warmup_days=0)
    dates_cut, q_cut, tq_cut = panel_daily(ts_cut, o_cut, c_cut)
    d_cut = target_from_params(dates_cut, q_cut, tq_cut, BASE)
    full_s = pd.Series(base_d["w"], index=pd.Index(dates))
    cut_s = pd.Series(d_cut["w"], index=pd.Index(dates_cut))
    daily_max_diff = float((full_s.reindex(cut_s.index) - cut_s).abs().max())
    W_cut = build_weights(ts_cut, o_cut, c_cut)
    weight_prefix_equal = bool(np.array_equal(W_base[:len(ts_cut)], W_cut))

    # benchmarks
    tq_bench = bt.benchmark(c[i0:, 1], ts[i0:], BARS)
    qq_bench = bt.benchmark(c[i0:, 0], ts[i0:], BARS)
    bil_bench = bt.benchmark(c[i0:, 2], ts[i0:], BARS)

    out = dict(
        agent="fast-trend-vol",
        status=("dev_pass" if (primary["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0.3672 and
                               primary["1bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229)
                else "dev_fail"),
        window=dict(start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END, sessions=int(len(bt.day_bounds(ts)[1])),
                    marks="1-minute", fills="next-open", band=0.02),
        verdict=dict(
            bar_cagr=0.3672, bar_max_drawdown=0.8229, bar_sharpe=0.82,
            passes_bar=bool(primary["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0.3672 and
                            primary["1bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229),
            meets_dd_target=bool(primary["1bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.60),
            cagr_minus_bar_pp=float((primary["1bp"]["cagr"] - 0.3672) * 100),
            dd_minus_bar_pp=float((0.8229 - primary["1bp"]["max_drawdown"]) * 100),
        ),
        primary=dict(params=BASE, intraday_stops=int(n_stops),
                     **{"1bp": primary["1bp"], "5bp": primary["5bp"],
                        "10bp": primary["10bp"]}),
        grid=grid_out,
        ablations=ablations,
        neighbourhood=neighbourhood,
        baseline_165d_benchmark_only=bench_165,
        lag_placebo=lag_out,
        random_run_placebo=dict(draws=placebo, summary=placebo_summary),
        cut_tests=cuts,
        subperiods=sub,
        causality=dict(daily_target_max_abs_diff=daily_max_diff,
                       weight_prefix_equal=weight_prefix_equal),
        benchmarks=dict(tqqq_buy_hold=tq_bench, qqq_buy_hold=qq_bench,
                        bil_buy_hold=bil_bench),
        notes=dict(
            tqqq_exposure="mean TQQQ weight over all 1m bars",
            calibrated_exposure="bt.stats exposure; 1.0 because BIL is an asset",
            old_base="165d QQQ SMA + 4% TQQQ stop is deliberately not used",
            holdout="2024-2026 not loaded",
        ),
    )
    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))

    # concise console summary
    print("\n== primary ==")
    for k in ("1bp", "5bp", "10bp"):
        m = primary[k]
        print(f"{k:4s} CAGR {m['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {m['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {m['sharpe']:4.2f}  TQQQ {m['tqqq_exposure']*100:4.1f}%  "
              f"fills {m['fills']}")
    print("\n== grid ==")
    for name, v in grid_out.items():
        print(f"{name:10s} CAGR {v['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {v['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {v['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print("\n== ablations ==")
    for name, v in ablations.items():
        print(f"{name:22s} CAGR {v['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {v['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {v['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print("\n== neighbourhood ==")
    for name, v in neighbourhood.items():
        print(f"{name:12s} CAGR {v['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {v['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {v['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print("\n== placebo ==")
    print(placebo_summary)
    print("\n== causality ==")
    print(out["causality"])
    print(f"\ndone {time.time()-t0:.0f}s -> {HERE/'result.json'}")
